items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: Hey, Harry! Oh yes, we're coming in to hear the piano player.

ctx.x: So I heard about him, but... One night, I was walking on Seventh Avenue, and on 136th Street they were having a party, a birthday party...whichever... Either it was a house rent party or a birthday party, whichever it was. And I heard this piano coming from outside the window. Somebody said, "Listen, that's Art Tatum playing in there." Then the name struck me, you know. I went over on 136th Street, and it was on the ground floor. So the person said, "What do you want?" And I stuck my foot in the door, which was a…

Everybody was dancing. So I looked around at the people. The couples were dancing. And I saw the keys coming up, but I didn't see the hands! I saw the keys coming up. Like, he had made an impression... He was so fast that the keys were still trembling. You know, they were (?)! So I heard "Tea For Two," and it sounded like two pianos, you know. I looked for the other piano; it wasn't there.
